story: Drona, a brahmin master of weapons, became the teacher of the Kaurava and Pandava princes. He loved Arjuna as his best student and his own son Ashwatthama most of all. In the war he led the Kaurava army after Bhishma fell.
belief: Dronacharya is honoured as the great teacher, and India's top award for sports coaches is named after him. His story also raises hard questions about how teachers treat their students.
turns: He demanded Ekalavya's thumb as his fee so that Arjuna would stay the best. He used his students to take revenge on his old friend Drupada. When falsely told that Ashwatthama was dead, he put down his weapons and was killed.
facts: He was born from a pot (drona), which gives him his name.
Gurugram is traditionally said to be the village given to him as guru.
He was killed by Dhrishtadyumna, Drupada's son.
lessons: A teacher's duty is to every student.
Revenge carried out through others still stains you.
more: His childhood friend Drupada, once king, humiliated him by refusing to treat him as an equal.
As his teaching fee, he asked his students to capture Drupada, and Arjuna did.
